source_user: Give one misleading intuition about pipeline parallelism and correct it. Case variant 5: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Pipeline parallelism partitions layers across stages and can require microbatching to reduce pipeline bubbles.
corrected_answer: Use a matched baseline and change only the pipeline setting. Fix model weights, precision, device count/topology, stage partition, schedule, microbatch count, batch size, prompt/output lengths, concurrency, software versions, and warm-up. Mechanism: microbatches move through stages, allowing a later stage to compute while an earlier stage handles another microbatch; this can reduce idle bubbles but adds activation transfers and synchronization. Measure TTFT, inter-token latency p50/p95/p99, throughput/goodput, stage compute/transfer/wait time, utilization, peak per-stage memory, errors/OOMs, and output correctness over repeated trials. Boundary: do not infer interactive-latency gains from saturated throughput; low concurrency, short sequences, stage imbalance, slow links, or fill/drain bubbles can make pipeline parallelism slower.
risks: Pipeline throughput and latency are workload- and load-dependent; aggregate means can hide stage imbalance, queueing, tail latency, or failures.
